name: Chemistry
notes: Meets the requirements for an American Chemical Society (ACS) approved degree.
At least 55 credit hours in chemistry and at least 85 credit hours overall. A 2.0 GPA must be maintained in the major, excluding allied field courses.

Both general/organic sequences require CHEM 210W (unlike the BA, where CHEM 208 is an alternative). The standard sequence also requires CHEM 132, which the first-year organic sequence does not - CHEM 132 is therefore part of the sequence rather than the theory group.

CHEM 231, 232, or 244 may be replaced by an upper-level laboratory course from another department that maintains ACS curricular coverage in analytical, physical, and macromolecular/nanoscale chemistry - substitutions are not modeled.

Senior research is two semesters totalling eight credits of CHEM 393, plus a written thesis read and approved by the research advisor and a second chemistry faculty member. The app places CHEM 393 once; the second semester is not separately represented.
Biochemistry may be taken as CHEM 262, BIOL 250, or BIOL 252.

requirementGroups.label: General and organic chemistry sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: General Standard Sequence: CHEM 131; CHEM 132; CHEM 203; CHEM 204; CHEM 207; CHEM 210W. First-year Organic Sequence: CHEM 131; CHEM 171; CHEM 172; CHEM 173; CHEM 210W

requirementGroups.label: Theory courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Theory Courses (16 credits): CHEM 211: Inorganic Chemistry; CHEM 251: Physical Chemistry I; CHEM 252: Physical Chemistry II

requirementGroups.label: Core laboratory courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Both of the core laboratory courses: CHEM 231: Chemical Instrumentation; CHEM 234: Advanced Laboratory Techniques

requirementGroups.label: Physical chemistry laboratory
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One physical chemistry lab course: CHEM 232: Molecular Spectroscopy OR CHEM 244: Adv. Nuclear Science (ANSEL)

requirementGroups.label: 400-level chemistry course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: 400-Level/Graduate Level Chemistry Course (4 credits). At least four credits of a 400-level chemistry course may be taken anytime during the junior or senior year.

requirementGroups.label: Senior research
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Senior Research (8 credits): CHEM 393: Senior Thesis Research. Two semesters, equaling eight credit hours of Senior Research, are required for a BS degree.
requirementGroups.note: Two semesters are required; the app places the course once.

requirementGroups.label: Calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following sequences: MATH 141, MATH 142, and MATH 143; MATH 161 and MATH 162

requirementGroups.label: Linear algebra or differential equations
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Plus one of the following courses: MATH 165: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations; MATH 163: Ordinary Differential Equations

requirementGroups.label: Additional mathematics, statistics, or computing
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Plus one of the following courses: MATH 164: Multidimensional Calculus; STAT 180; STAT 190; STAT 201: Introduction to Probability; CSC 161; CSC 171; Any 200-level mathematics course
requirementGroups.note: The 'any 200-level mathematics course' alternative is not modeled.

requirementGroups.label: Physics sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Physics Coursework (8 credits). One of the following sequences: PHYS 113-114 Sequence (General Physics I & II); PHYS 121-123 Sequence (Mechanics and Electricity & Magnetism) recommended

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses (at least one in chemistry)
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: All chemistry majors are required to complete two upper-level writing courses ('W' courses). At least one of these courses must be a chemistry department course selected from the following: CHEM 210W; CHEM 231W; CHEM 232W; CHEM 234W.
upperLevelWriting.note: Only one of the two must be a chemistry course; the second may come from another department.
